classification.difficultyReason: Combine equal radii, isosceles base angles, parallel-line angles and triangle or quadrilateral angle sums.

content.prompt: Find $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ and $\theta$ in each diagram, giving reasons.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with matching ticks on AB and BC; 25 degrees at C, alpha at A and beta at B.

answer.worked:
$AB=BC$, so $\alpha=25^\circ$ (base angles of an isosceles triangle).
$$\begin{align*}\beta&=180^\circ-25^\circ-25^\circ\\\beta&=130^\circ\end{align*}$$
The interior angles of $\triangle ABC$ sum to $180^\circ$.

spec.description: Triangle FGH with equal FG and FH, external 24-degree label pointing into angle F, and gamma at G.

answer.worked:
$FG=FH$, so $\angle FGH=\angle GHF$ (base angles of an isosceles triangle).
$$\begin{align*}\gamma&=(180^\circ-24^\circ)\div2\\\gamma&=78^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Circle with highlighted centre O, radii OA and OB, chord AB, central angle 110 degrees and theta at A.

answer.worked:
$OA=OB$ (radii), so $\triangle AOB$ is isosceles and its base angles are equal.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=(180^\circ-110^\circ)\div2\\\theta&=35^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Circle with diameters PS and QR through O; chords PQ and RS marked parallel; 20 degrees at PQR, alpha at QPS and beta at QRS.
spec.mathematics: OP=OQ; PQ parallel RS; angle PQR=20 degrees.

answer.short:
$\alpha=\beta=20^\circ$.

Use equal radii and alternate angles.
answer.worked:
$OP=OQ$ (radii), so $\triangle POQ$ is isosceles. Since $Q$, $O$ and $R$ are collinear, $\angle PQO=20^\circ$. Therefore $\alpha=20^\circ$ (equal base angles).
$\beta=20^\circ$ (alternate angles, $PQ\parallel RS$, with transversal $QR$).

spec.description: Quadrilateral DEFG with 100 degrees at D, theta at E, 70 degrees at F and a right-angle square at G.

answer.worked:
The interior angles of quadrilateral $DEFG$ sum to $360^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=360^\circ-100^\circ-70^\circ-90^\circ\\\theta&=100^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Four extended straight lines XABY, PDCQ, FADG and HBCI, without parallel marks. Exterior angles XAF=98 degrees, HBY=92 degrees and PDG=105 degrees; theta is QCI.
spec.mathematics: Vertically opposite angles supply three interior angles of quadrilateral ABCD and identify theta with its fourth angle.
spec.answerVisibility: Theta remains unknown; no parallel relationship is added.

answer.short:
$\theta=65^\circ$.

Use vertically opposite angles and the angle sum of quadrilateral $ABCD$.
answer.worked:
$\angle DAB=98^\circ$, $\angle ABC=92^\circ$ and $\angle ADC=105^\circ$ (vertically opposite angles).
$$\begin{align*}\angle BCD&=360^\circ-98^\circ-92^\circ-105^\circ\\\angle BCD&=65^\circ\end{align*}$$
The interior angles of quadrilateral $ABCD$ sum to $360^\circ$. Hence $\theta=65^\circ$ (vertically opposite angles at $C$).
